CriticalAlgorithms_Algorithmic_Bias_Visu.inherited: From QFEP_Synthesis: Post-crisis begins with representation itself. After learning to name a model’s choices, ask whose distinctions those choices make clear and whose they compress.
CriticalAlgorithms_Algorithmic_Bias_Visu.question: Which differences disappear when a representation gives some terms less room?
CriticalAlgorithms_Algorithmic_Bias_Visu.ontology: An embedding represents items by positions; distances can make distinctions available or collapse them. This artifact is an authored spatial analogy, not a measured embedding from a trained model.
CriticalAlgorithms_Algorithmic_Bias_Visu.experiment: Choose two warm-coloured word labels and follow both as you move PERSPECTIVE. Compare their separation with two grey labels.
CriticalAlgorithms_Algorithmic_Bias_Visu.observe: Warm labels compress into a small region while grey labels spread out and move away. Label positions and visual emphasis change together.
CriticalAlgorithms_Algorithmic_Bias_Visu.limit: The model makes compression legible but does not establish that these exact distances occur in an actual language model. Its two preselected term groups also deserve scrutiny.
CriticalAlgorithms_Algorithmic_Bias_Visu.variation: Existing: stop halfway and track one distinction still visible and one becoming difficult to read. Proposed: compare these authored positions with a documented measured embedding and several different groupings.
CriticalAlgorithms_Algorithmic_Bias_Visu.handoff: The applied-ethics room moves from word positions to furniture. A plan can distribute the ability to participate before anyone begins speaking.
open_questions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.
Do not call this an actual trained embedding, an empirical bias measurement, or a visitor camera transform.

CriticalAlgorithms_Applied_Ethics.inherited: From CriticalAlgorithms_Algorithmic_Bias_Visualization: The applied-ethics room moves from word positions to furniture. A plan can distribute the ability to participate before anyone begins speaking.
CriticalAlgorithms_Applied_Ethics.question: Who is made easiest to address before anybody has spoken?
CriticalAlgorithms_Applied_Ethics.ontology: An affordance makes some actions easier than others. A seating plan distributes visibility, orientation and the symbolic position of a head.
CriticalAlgorithms_Applied_Ethics.experiment: Walk around the paired room models. Trace a line of sight from the head chair in the long-table plan, then from one chair in the circular plan.
CriticalAlgorithms_Applied_Ethics.observe: One model singles out a head position; the other arranges chairs around a shared centre. Red and green colours already suggest an evaluation.
CriticalAlgorithms_Applied_Ethics.limit: A circle does not guarantee equal speech, access or authority. Colour can supply the answer before the learner has examined the arrangement.
CriticalAlgorithms_Applied_Ethics.variation: Existing: defend one useful role for the head position and identify one exclusion the circle could retain. Proposed: test sightlines and turn-taking with actual groups, including mobility and hearing needs.
CriticalAlgorithms_Applied_Ethics.handoff: The next room lets two requirements meet without immediately deleting one. Participation can be shared while the resulting claims still conflict.
open_questions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.
Models are miniatures, not functional visitor seats; no toggle interaction exists. Do not claim geometry alone determines politics.

SpeculativeComputation_Paraconsistent_En.inherited: From CriticalAlgorithms_Applied_Ethics: The next room lets two requirements meet without immediately deleting one. Participation can be shared while the resulting claims still conflict.
SpeculativeComputation_Paraconsistent_En.question: Must one account disappear before two accounts can share a system?
SpeculativeComputation_Paraconsistent_En.ontology: Two branches preserve distinct versions; a conflict records incompatibility requiring a policy. Retaining provenance differs from silently choosing a winner.
SpeculativeComputation_Paraconsistent_En.experiment: Inspect the two labelled pillars and the lit junction between them. Trace each branch to the meeting point before deciding what a combined result should retain.
SpeculativeComputation_Paraconsistent_En.observe: Branch A and branch B remain visible around a pulsing conflict marker. The default junction does not resolve either version.
SpeculativeComputation_Paraconsistent_En.limit: Disagreement between records is not automatically a logical contradiction. Formal paraconsistency requires inference rules that avoid arbitrary conclusions from a contradiction; the sculpture does not implement those rules.
SpeculativeComputation_Paraconsistent_En.variation: Existing thought experiment: assign the branches two incompatible dated measurements and preserve source and time before choosing a policy. Proposed: a small rule table showing which inferences survive a contradiction.
SpeculativeComputation_Paraconsistent_En.handoff: Situated computation takes up that provenance. Four panels will judge one subject differently, and their positions will become part of what the judgement tells you.
open_questions: The merge-conflict sculpture is an analogy. Add a small visible inference table that retains a contradiction without deriving an unrelated conclusion.
Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.
Central formal-logic encounter is currently a diagram, not a paraconsistent computation. Add explicit rule example before claiming the room teaches formal inference.
Try the written encounter in the actual museum, alone and with a group. Check visibility, reach, the stated response and the handoff before accepting a room baseline.

SpeculativeComputation_Situated_Computat.inherited: From SpeculativeComputation_Paraconsistent_Engineering: Situated computation takes up that provenance. Four panels will judge one subject differently, and their positions will become part of what the judgement tells you.
SpeculativeComputation_Situated_Computat.question: What changes when the subject stays the same but the source of the verdict changes?
SpeculativeComputation_Situated_Computat.ontology: A claim has a subject, a predicate, confidence and provenance. Four authored viewpoints attach different evaluations to the same subject identifier.
SpeculativeComputation_Situated_Computat.experiment: Read the subject ID on all four panels, then compare each verdict, confidence and footer. Keep the identical subject fixed in your comparison.
SpeculativeComputation_Situated_Computat.observe: SUBJECT #4729 is ORDERLY 87%, CREATIVE 64%, DANGEROUS 92% or IRRELEVANT 22%, depending on the panel. Each panel names its viewpoint.
SpeculativeComputation_Situated_Computat.limit: These percentages are authored signs, not calibrated probabilities. Different judgements can have unequal evidence; situatedness does not make every verdict equally credible.
SpeculativeComputation_Situated_Computat.variation: Existing: choose the highest confidence and ask what extra evidence would make it trustworthy. Proposed: reveal distinct measurement criteria and allow one same observation to be evaluated under each.
SpeculativeComputation_Situated_Computat.handoff: Collective knowledge asks how contributions from different positions can become a common object without losing the evidence and disagreement that make it revisable.
open_questions: The four panels supply fixed viewpoints and percentages. Give each a stated criterion and observation before teaching an actual classification comparison.

SpeculativeComputation_Collective_Knowle.inherited: From SpeculativeComputation_Situated_Computation: Collective knowledge asks how contributions from different positions can become a common object without losing the evidence and disagreement that make it revisable.
SpeculativeComputation_Collective_Knowle.question: When many marks accumulate, what makes the result knowledge rather than a pile?
SpeculativeComputation_Collective_Knowle.ontology: A contribution is an event from a source; a shared artifact accumulates contributions. Participation counts and validation are different operations.
SpeculativeComputation_Collective_Knowle.experiment: Follow a packet from a rim node to the central structure. Compare how the edit and contributor readouts change during the first growing structure.
SpeculativeComputation_Collective_Knowle.observe: Packets from twelve peer positions add facets to a central helix. Repeated contributions can increase edits without introducing a new contributor.
SpeculativeComputation_Collective_Knowle.limit: The animation omits review, disagreement, exclusion and correction. The same rule accepting every contribution also accepts error; growing shape alone does not establish shared knowledge.
SpeculativeComputation_Collective_Knowle.variation: Existing: count several contributions from an already seen peer. Proposed: tag a disputed contribution and make acceptance, revision and source history visible.
SpeculativeComputation_Collective_Knowle.handoff: The rhizome will make the pattern of connection itself grow. A shared result can have many contributors while its network still develops uneven centres.

SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network.inherited: From SpeculativeComputation_Collective_Knowledge: The rhizome will make the pattern of connection itself grow. A shared result can have many contributors while its network still develops uneven centres.
SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network.question: Can a network grow through local connections without being given a root?
SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network.ontology: A graph has nodes and edges; this growth rule adds a spatial node and links it to nearby existing nodes. No root field or parent-child hierarchy is assigned.
SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network.experiment: Follow one new shoot and count its new links. Watch a locally crowded area and compare how often it receives a connection with a sparse area.
SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network.observe: Nodes and connecting segments accumulate while the NODES and EDGES readout changes. The structure restarts when its forty-node capacity is reached.
SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network.limit: Having no designated root does not guarantee equal influence or resilience. Early or centrally located nodes can collect many links.
SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network.variation: Existing: identify a visually busy node and predict the effect of losing it. Proposed: remove it and compute components instead of assuming the network remains connected.
SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network.handoff: The assembly laboratory adds a catalogue and a target arrangement. When connections must form a recognisable body, we can ask which bodies the catalogue has already imagined.

AdvancedLaboratory_Lab_Equipment_Simulat.inherited: From SpeculativeComputation_Rhizome_Network: The assembly laboratory adds a catalogue and a target arrangement. When connections must form a recognisable body, we can ask which bodies the catalogue has already imagined.
AdvancedLaboratory_Lab_Equipment_Simulat.question: How can the same inventory become more than one recognisable body?
AdvancedLaboratory_Lab_Equipment_Simulat.ontology: A catalogue names part types; an assembly assigns typed parts to target transforms and declares bonds. Motion towards targets is a separate mechanism from the chosen assembly.
AdvancedLaboratory_Lab_Equipment_Simulat.experiment: Choose a recognisable part and follow it through floating and assembly phases. Wait for another assembly and compare which relations have changed.
AdvancedLaboratory_Lab_Equipment_Simulat.observe: Forty pieces float, then move towards target positions; bond lines update between assigned parts. The scene cycles assemblies with ten-second float and assembly phases.
AdvancedLaboratory_Lab_Equipment_Simulat.limit: A part name or bond line does not establish molecular chemistry. Predefined bodies can be recombined without making every possible body available.
AdvancedLaboratory_Lab_Equipment_Simulat.variation: Existing: compare a named part’s role across two automatic arrangements. Proposed: author an assembly that the present catalogue makes awkward, then decide whether to change the inventory or its connection rules.
AdvancedLaboratory_Lab_Equipment_Simulat.handoff: The final ledger asks us to record the consequences of those choices. A useful catalogue permits construction while also defining what its builder has to struggle to express.
open_questions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.

PostCrisis_Synthesis.inherited: From AdvancedLaboratory_Lab_Equipment_Simulation: The final ledger asks us to record the consequences of those choices. A useful catalogue permits construction while also defining what its builder has to struggle to express.
PostCrisis_Synthesis.question: Can you name one person a useful design choice could leave out?
PostCrisis_Synthesis.ontology: A decision has an intended benefit, an excluded case and an owner who can revisit it. Accountability needs a record and a subsequent response, not merely a confession.
PostCrisis_Synthesis.experiment: Read one complete choice/exclusion pair before it scrolls away. State a specific change that would reduce that exclusion and one trade-off it would introduce.
PostCrisis_Synthesis.observe: Example pairs such as a short name field and long names appear on the ledger; older lines leave the six-line display as new entries arrive.
PostCrisis_Synthesis.limit: Naming exclusion cannot substitute for changing the condition that produces it. The prewritten groups are prompts, not evidence about a particular user.
PostCrisis_Synthesis.variation: Existing discussion: return to one museum room and name one real rule, the encounter it prevents and a test for a proposed change. Proposed build: save that decision with its source, owner and next review.
PostCrisis_Synthesis.handoff: Go back to a chosen room with one question, one proposed change and one observable consequence. The museum’s next version begins with that specific return.
open_questions: The ledger scrolls examples rather than saving a visitor's decisions. A later live ledger should preserve one choice, its evidence, the proposed repair and its observed result.
